usage: This is the standard greeting used from late afternoon until late at night. It is universally understood across Morocco and is appropriate for both formal and casual situations. You can use it when entering a shop, greeting friends at a cafe, or arriving at someone's home in the evening.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Use this when addressing more than one person.

variants.label: warm greeting
variants.note: A slightly warmer alternative often used among friends or as a reply.

variants.label: to one person
variants.note: Adds a personal touch when greeting a single individual.

responses.english: may God give you a good evening

examples.arabic: مسا لخير، واش كاين شي خبز؟
examples.transliteration: msa lkhir, wash kayn shi khubz?
examples.english: Good evening, is there any bread?

examples.arabic: مسا لخير عليكم، كيف داز نهاركم؟
examples.english: Good evening everyone, how was your day?
Good evening sir, please come in.
